documents.title: Policy 100-022: Howard University Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy
documents.summary: Howard's formal university-wide AI policy (effective April 2026), owned by the Provost. It sets general requirements (legal compliance, verifying outputs, context-dependent disclosure, no confidential data or PII in AI systems, no training on university data), and has sections on teaching, research, external partnerships, and work use. For teaching, faculty must state permissible and impermissible AI use in syllabi, and students must ask the instructor when guidance is missing.

documents.title: Initial Howard University Guidelines for use of Generative AI Tools
documents.summary: The Provost's initial (2023) guidelines on generative AI, framed as values and recommendations rather than rules. They stress bias and misinformation risks especially for the African Diaspora, privacy, AI literacy, transparency, verifying AI output, and ethical and labor implications. Schools, departments, and faculty are told to write their own discipline-specific policies with clear expectations and penalties, and the guidelines call for fairness in policing AI use.

units.policy: Generative AI is often conflated with Artificial General Intelligence (an autonomous, sentient intelligence), which it is not.

units.anchor: Generative AI refers to computer systems that produce various forms of human expression
units.policy: Generative AI refers to computer systems that produce forms of human expression such as written summaries, composite images, videos, music, or vocal mimicry.

units.anchor: through word-processing spelling and grammar checkers
units.policy: Generative AI continues a history of technological aids many already use, such as word-processing spelling and grammar checkers and automated guides built into phones and tablets.

units.anchor: writing and voice production remain important modes of critical, artistic, and sense-based learning
units.policy: Values and guidelines are needed because writing and voice production remain important modes of critical, artistic, and sense-based learning vital to understanding and cognitive development.

units.anchor: represent a concerted shift to our learning practices and definitions of integrity
units.policy: Tools such as ChatGPT represent a concerted shift in learning practices and definitions of integrity, and thus require informed engagement.

units.policy: The guidelines give information and recommendations for faculty, students, and other stakeholders on learning and engaging these tools in academic settings.

units.policy: AI models fail to grasp the diverse nuances of human opinion, thought, and language, especially within the African Diaspora.

units.policy: AI technologies frequently echo dominant viewpoints of certain groups, spread misinformation, or present inaccurate information as fact.

units.policy: The University expects students and faculty to adhere to the highest ethical and moral standards of conduct.

units.policy: The popularity of generative AI demands an expansive set of AI literacies developed across colleges, disciplines, departments, and programs.

documents.summary: CETLA's teaching page that supplements Policy 100-022. It restates the policy's definitions and splits responsibilities among faculty (state AI rules in the syllabus, protect student records), students (follow course rules, disclose when required, ask when unclear, own their work), and all users (verify output, consider bias and IP). It offers a three-level syllabus template (Disallowed, Restricted, Unrestricted), recommended additions for syllabus statements, a responsible-AI checklist, and an overview of AI tools.

notes: Coder A dry run. Only university-layer documents exist (school, computing, course none-found per collect file). Policy 100-022 is institution-wide and covers research, external partnerships, and work use as well as teaching; all AI provisions were coded. CETLA tier template coded both as a P05 tier list and as individual tier rules, matching the approach used for Oregon State. Descriptive product blurbs on the CETLA page (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Firefly, Gamma) were not coded as they state no policy; GitHub Copilot and agentic AI descriptions were coded under P07 because they bear on IDE/agent coverage.
